title: Hotel Website
description: A full resort or hotel site — how it works, what you configure, and commands to generate your project.

blocks.text: The hotel template targets boutique hotels, resorts, and homestays that need room listings, gallery, facilities, reviews, and enquiry flows — not a generic landing page. Visitors browse room types, open enquiry modals, and see contact details driven from a single config file. Staff manage content through /admin without touching code for day-to-day updates.

Hotel sites repeat the same patterns: hero with property story, room grid with categories, gallery, amenities list, guest reviews, sticky phone/WhatsApp, and lead capture. This template encodes those patterns so you focus on brand copy, photography, and pricing — not rebuilding admin CRUD and enquiry plumbing.

blocks.title: Demo brand
blocks.text: The default content models Lakeside Haven Resort in Lonavala. Replace names, URLs, and images — the structure stays the same.

items: Next.js 16 App Router with React 19 and TypeScript
Room types with slug pages (e.g. /rooms/deluxe-lake-view) and enquiry modals
Gallery and facilities managed in admin
Promo banner and optional LeadRat CRM hook
Prisma + MariaDB with Docker Compose for local dev
FTP pipeline for uploading room and hero assets

blocks.text: Besides standard brand fields (name, URL, phone, email, address), hotel init supports tagline, operator/developer name, channel partner label, and templeDistance — a short line about a nearby landmark (lake, temple, viewpoint) shown in contact sections. Real-estate templates use RERA instead; you won't see --temple-distance there.

Use the builder below to produce a copy-paste command for quick copy, interactive setup, or a fully customized non-interactive run. Pick generate new project, then walk through options, theme, brand, and database — skip any field you don't need yet.
